newsitem.title: CHINA: Bank of East Asia to widen income sources.
newsitem.headline: Bank of East Asia to widen income sources.

text.p: With property-related loans threatening to take up an ever larger portion of its loan portfolio, Bank of East Asia Ltd will continue its efforts to diversify its income sources, senior executives said on Friday.
Hong Kong's positive economic outlook will help the bank achieve this goal, they said.

"The upswing in local economic activity is likely to be sustained in the second half of 1997. Consumer and investment spending is expected to expand further," said chairman David Li at a news conference to announce the bank's results for the first six months of the year.

In the second half of the year, the bank will emphasize expanding its trade financing and loan syndication operations while also targeting new corporate customers including Hong Kong-based mainland companies, executives said.
The bank announced profit attributable to shareholders of HK$1.03 billion for the six months ended June 30, 1997, a 21.7 percent increase over the year-earlier period.
The results were significantly better than market expectations.

Interest income rose 16.93 percent to HK$4.26 billion, but interest expense jumped by 18.30 percent to HK$2.66 billion, with the result that net interest income rose by 14.73 percent, the chairman's statement said.

"During the first half, funding costs increased as growth in Hong Kong dollar deposits lagged behind those of Hong Kong dollar loans, while the upward trend of U.S. interest rates pushed Hong Kong dollar interest rates higher," the statement said.
"However, growth in domestic lending volume was more than enough to offset the slight increase in funding costs," it said.
Loans and advances to customers rose by 33 percent.

The results were also boosted by a 23.50 percent increase in non-interest income to HK$568.67 million and included at the net income level HK$65 million in profits from securities trading, said senior general manager Samson Li who also manages the bank's securities trading operations.
Operating expenses rose 14.1 percent, but the bank still managed to lower its cost-to-income ratio to 37.3 percent compared with 38.2 percent in first half 1996, the chairman said.
In the first half of the year, the bank issued certificates of deposit totalling HK$5.55 billion, nearly tripling the bank's outstanding CDs to HK$12.4 billion compared with a year ago.

The issue of CDs, a practice actively adopted by many local banks in the past year, provided a source of deposits that was less expensive and more stable than wholesale deposits from corporate customers, analysts said.

The bank expanded its Hong Kong branch network to 95 branches during the period. Its Taiwan office was upgraded to a branch status in May and representative offices were opened in Labuan, Malaysia in February, in Kuala Lumpur in June, and in Birmingham, England and Manila, Philippines on August 1.
The Bank of East Asia closed HK$0.10 lower at HK$32.10 on Friday.
